messages:
sophie: quick heads-up. while bringing up t5-chat-4b I hit a HF->Redwood chat_template conversion bug. conditional system block gets removed and the assistant sentinel disappears when the block is false, shifting role token indices and causing small but consistent quality drops.
ev an: ack. can you paste the minimal HF template that reproduces it?
sophie: here you go — HF Jinja:
```
{% if system_prompt %}
{"role": "system", "content": "{{ system_prompt }}"}
{% endif %}
{"role": "user", "content": "{{ user_input }}"}
```
Converted RW prompt becomes a bare user line with no assistant marker in the empty-block case, e.g. the assistant sentinel is missing.
diego: that smells like the converter is trimming empty blocks and not emitting placeholder role markers. have we checked tokenizer special tokens?
sophie: good point. model config.json for the variant doesn't declare role sentinels, and tokenizer wasn't patched with additional_special_tokens, so indices shifted silently. repro token views:
```
# before: ... <SYSTEM> ... <ASSISTANT> ...
# after:  ... <SYSTEM> ...
```
which removes the index used by KV cache mapping.
mia: explains why the micro-eval convo-turn scores dropped ~1% across KL/next-token accuracy on the small benchmark we ran after quant-4bit onboarding.
samir: quant adds another twist — quantized embedding tables expect stable token indexes. if a sentinel gets removed the embedding lookup offsets can produce odd logits, especially under 4-bit QAT-style transforms.
evan: short-term fixes: (1) ensure tokenizer.add_special_tokens includes explicit role tokens in convert step, (2) render jinja with trim_blocks=False and lstrip_blocks=False so empty blocks still output placeholders, or inject a zero-width placeholder `{{ system_prompt or '\u200B' }}`.
sophie: here's a quick onboarding script patch suggestion:
```
# in hf->rw convert
tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<|system|>", "<|assistant|>", "<|user|>"]})
model.config.update({"chat": {"role_tokens": {"system": "<|system|>", "assistant": "<|assistant|>", "user": "<|user|>"}}})
```
also set Jinja env: `Environment(trim_blocks=False, lstrip_blocks=False)`.
diego: we should also avoid relying solely on string heuristics in the converter. better to have it always emit explicit sentinel tokens for each role slot, even if content is empty.
infra-bot: deploy-check: onboarding-tests/conv-turns FAILED for t5-chat-4b quant-4bit at stage 3 due to message-boundary token mismatch.
mia: proposing a unit test that compares token ids between: (A) HF rendered template and (B) HF->RW converted prompt. fail if shapes or ids differ. tiny script:
```
def compare(hf_tmpl, ctx):
  hf_r = jinja_env.render(hf_tmpl, **ctx)
  rw_p = hf_to_rw(hf_tmpl, **ctx)
  return tokenizer(hf_r).ids, tokenizer(rw_p).ids
```
if mismatch -> fail onboarding.
samir: add quant-mode checks: run the same comparison on quantized model artifacts to catch index-offset issues that only show up post-quant.
sophie: TL;DR: root cause is twofold -> (1) Jinja empty/conditional blocks collapsing during conversion, (2) missing explicit role special tokens in config/tokenizer leading to downstream index shifts under quant. short-term: add special tokens + make jinja preserve placeholders. long-term: change converter to always emit explicit role sentinels and add the token-shape unit test to the onboarding pipeline.
evan: I'll open a small PR with converter guard + unit test and tag @sophie @mia for review.
sophie: added a checklist item to the model bring-up doc: "verify chat_template empty-block preservation + token-id parity vs HF render" and linked the micro-eval that showed the regression. :thumbsup:
